Functional Equations Problem Set

Key Methods

  • Substitution Method (Value Assignment)
    Substitute specific values to uncover properties of the function.
  • Finding Special Values
    First determine the values of the function at key points to deduce its overall properties.
  • Induction Method
    Inductive chain: .
  • Change of Variables (Substitution)
    Simplify steps and reveal the essential structure of the function through variable substitution.
  • Iterative Method
    If the value of is known, iteration can be applied.
  • Injectivity and Surjectivity Analysis
    Both injectivity and surjectivity are strong properties. Proving injectivity allows removing from both sides; proving surjectivity allows freely substituting special values into the image.
  • Monotonicity and Bounding Method
    Deriving a contradiction by bounding values is a technique I am relatively good at. Sometimes it can also be used to prove monotonicity.
  • Asymmetric Swap Method
    By swapping and in an expression that is symmetric on one side but asymmetric on the other, function properties can be simplified.
  • Permutation Cycle Method
    If the function is clearly related to permutation cycles, consider permutation cycles and fixed points.
  • Even/Odd Decomposition Transformation
    Similar to other transformations, decomposing a function into the sum of an even function and an odd function can simplify the problem.
